test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Ramesh can complete a piece of work alone in 16 days and Suresh can complete the same piece of work alone in 10 days. They started the work together, but Ramesh had to leave 4 days before the completion of the work. In how many days will the work get completed?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Let total work be **LCM(16, 10) = 80 units**.

Efficiency of **Ramesh = 5** and **Suresh = 8**.

Since **Ramesh leaves 4 days early**, add his 4-day potential work to the total: 80 + (5 × 4) = 100 units.

Total days = Adjusted Work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 100 ÷ (5 + 8) = 100/13 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 7(9/13) days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Ramesh** alone takes 16 days, **Suresh** alone takes 10 days.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency**
 **Ramesh** 16 80 5
 **Suresh** 10 8
**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total work be completed in **x days**.

⇒ **Ramesh** worked for (x − 4) days and **Suresh** worked for x days.

⇒ Work done by **Ramesh** + Work done by **Suresh** = 80

⇒ 5 × (x − 4) + 8 × x = 80

⇒ 5x − 20 + 8x = 80

⇒ 13x = 100

⇒ x = 100/13 = 7(9/13) days

**∴ The correct answer is 7(9/13) days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Leaving Early vs Joining Late

If a person leaves **'n' days before completion**, add (n × efficiency) to total work. If a person joins **'n' days late**, it does not change the total work units but reduces their active time.

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar logic applies where efficiency of an **outlet pipe** is taken as negative, while an **inlet pipe** is positive.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the **actual work done** by each individual (Efficiency × Time).</p
